jQuery is a library that needs to introduction. However, every time I ask other devs about it they either love it or they hate it with a passion.

The main reason I have heard is that it's too bloated, it tries to do too much beyond the very useful selector functionality.

What do you think, voat?

To me it's a productivity booster. I could write out my own functionality but why reinvent the wheel?

Yeah, it's bloated but it's a tool box. It's capable of more than just DOM selection and manipulation. It makes AJAX operations smoother, animation of DOM elements, event handling, custom events. It does a lot and it lets you ignore browser inconsistencies so you can get work done.

I do agree that people can grow to dependent on it. I am guilty of that, but honestly, when your boss is throwing a fit because shit is taking a while, I'd much rather have something like jQuery at my disposal so I don't get snagged on all kinds of browser bugs. Some people say "well, jQuery has bugs too." Yeah, so does all software ever written, aside from "Hello World!" programs. I'll take jQuery's bugs over all the browser bugs any day.

when your boss is throwing a fit because shit is taking a while

This was my experience on a lot of agency projects. We weren't granted the time to build something clean and elegant, we used jQuery for everything, plugins for everything, and hacks for everything. The projects would become difficult to maintain and barely ship out the door in stable condition. So... I quit agencies and will never go back.
I feel like I'm looking into a mirror when I read your comment. Agencies are fucking awful.

For me it's simply old news. I still have it as a dependency but I'm pretty sure 90% of my application code no longer executes jQuery code. I don't have to support IE8, but hey neither does jQuery 2. Browsers are good enough now that native scripting is becoming good enough, or lighter libraries like Zepto or Angular's jqLite or acceptable. In my opinion the jQuery 3 release was pretty lackluster and might be one of the last recognizable releases. They're cleaning up the API quite well, but to me it's beginning to feel like the trailing end of old libraries like Prototype & Dojo.

For utilities I run lodash, but even that's getting old. I'm porting a lot of lodash features into ES6 JS code with the precompiler BabelJs. The dependencies are becoming less and less necessary virtually every week.

I LOVED jQuery in the days of old IE support. It was like a beacon of light shining down a dark tunnel. I still have one legacy app with a client that's entirely a modular jQuery app. I don't hate jQuery, I just don't have a need for it anymore.

However, one thing I do hate, is when backend developers call themselves full stack developers because they can install a couple jQuery plugins on the page and patch together a functional UI. In my experience those types of UI developers produce poor frontend code that's prone to bugs and difficult to maintain. I mean we all gotta start somewhere, but don't call yourself experienced in Javascript if you only copy & paste jQuery snippets to build the UI.
